# ClearPath

> Free, open-source browser extension that makes any website accessible — simplifies text, reads pages aloud with word highlighting, and overlays AAC symbols. No account required.

ClearPath is built for AAC users, people with dyslexia, and anyone who needs web content on their own terms. It works on top of any existing website — no cooperation from the site owner required.

## Key facts

- Price: free, no account required, no data collected
- Platforms: Chrome now (Manifest V3 browser extension); Firefox support is planned, launching after Chrome
- License: open source, MIT
- Privacy: Read Aloud, Reading Mode, Focus Tools, Symbol Overlay, and Vocabulary all work fully offline; Simplify requires your own LLM API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local Ollama instance) — there is no offline fallback for that one feature

## Features

- **Read Aloud** — text-to-speech with word-by-word highlighting, built into every page. Configurable voice, speed, pitch. Works offline.
- **Simplify** — right-click any text and rewrite it in plain English at Grade 3, 5, or 8 reading level. Requires your own LLM API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, or local Ollama).
- **Reading Mode** — strips pages down to their content, applies OpenDyslexic font, adjustable spacing and column width, four color themes (Light, Dark, Sepia, High Contrast).
- **Focus Tools** — a reading ruler that follows the cursor, paragraph focus mode, word-complexity highlighting with simpler alternatives on hover or keyboard focus.
- **Symbol Overlay** — displays AAC pictogram symbols above words using the open ARASAAC library.
- **Profiles** — save named accessibility configurations and export/import them as JSON, useful for SLPs and caregivers configuring a device for someone else.
- **Vocabulary** — double-click any word for an instant plain-English definition, powered by a bundled offline dictionary (21,000+ entries). No API key, no internet required.
